questionText:
Consider the following two syntax-directed definitions SDD1 and SDD2 for type declarations.

SDD1
Grammar (G1)Semantic Rules
$D \rightarrow T\,V$$D.type = T.type$
$V.type = T.type$
$T \rightarrow \text{int}$$T.type = \text{int}$
$T \rightarrow \text{float}$$T.type = \text{float}$
$V \rightarrow V_1\,\text{id}$$V_1.type = V.type$
$\text{put}(\text{id.entry}, V.type)$
$V \rightarrow \text{id}$$\text{put}(\text{id.entry}, V.type)$
SDD2
Grammar (G2)Semantic Rules
$D \rightarrow D_1\,\text{id}$$D.type = D_1.type$
$\text{put}(\text{id.entry}, D_1.type)$
$D \rightarrow T\,\text{id}$$D.type = T.type$
$\text{put}(\text{id.entry}, T.type)$
$T \rightarrow \text{int}$$T.type = \text{int}$
$T \rightarrow \text{float}$$T.type = \text{float}$


$D$ is the start symbol, and $\text{int}$, $\text{float}$ and $\text{id}$ are the three terminals. The non-terminal $V_1$ is the same as $V$ and the non-terminal $D_1$ is the same as $D$. Here, the subscript is used to differentiate the grammar symbols on the two sides of a production. The function $\text{put}$ updates the symbol table with the type information for an identifier.

Let P and Q be the languages specified by grammars G1 and G2, respectively.

Which of the following statements is/are true?
options: The languages P and Q are the same
SDD2 is S-attributed and contains only synthesized attributes
SDD1 is L-attributed and contains only inherited attributes
The specifications of SDD1 and SDD2 are such that the same entries get added to the symbol table
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Option A.
Both grammars $G_1$ and $G_2$ generate sequences consisting of a type specifier ($ ext{int}$ or $ ext{float}$) followed by one or more identifiers ($ ext{id}$). Thus, $P = L(G_1) = L(G_2) = Q$. Therefore, Option A is true.

Step 2: Analyze Option B.
In SDD2, all semantic rules compute attributes of head non-terminals using only attributes of their children nodes. Since all attributes are synthesized and evaluated bottom-up, SDD2 is S-attributed and contains only synthesized attributes. Therefore, Option B is true.

Step 3: Analyze Option C.
In SDD1, attributes such as $V.type$ and $V_1.type$ are inherited (passed top-down/sideways), but attributes such as $T.type$ and $D.type$ are synthesized. Because SDD1 contains both synthesized and inherited attributes, it does not contain only inherited attributes. Therefore, Option C is false.

Step 4: Analyze Option D.
For any valid declaration string, SDD1 passes the type information down through inherited attributes to call $ ext{put}( ext{id.entry}, ext{type})$, whereas SDD2 synthesizes the type information up to $D$ to perform the same $ ext{put}( ext{id.entry}, ext{type})$ action for each identifier. Thus, the exact same symbol table entries are created in both cases. Therefore, Option D is true.

Hence, options A, B, and D are true.
